name: Battle of Gettysburg

phases.title: Heth's brigades meet Buford's cavalry west of town
phases.text: Buford's cavalry held the ridges west of the town to delay the Confederates. Two of Heth's brigades, part of Hill's corps, came east along the Chambersburg Pike and met his dismounted troopers.

phases.title: The I Corps arrives as the cavalry falls back
phases.text: The Confederates pushed the Union cavalry east to McPherson Ridge. The vanguard of the I Corps then arrived and took up the fight beside it.

phases.title: Davis and Archer are repelled on McPherson Ridge
phases.text: North of the pike Davis won a brief success against Cutler's brigade but was repelled with heavy losses near an unfinished railroad cut. South of it Archer's brigade attacked through Herbst Woods and the Iron Brigade captured him.

phases.title: Pettigrew and Pender drive the I Corps back
phases.text: Heth's whole division engaged, with Pettigrew's brigade flanking the Union line, and Pender's division was added to the assault. The I Corps was driven back through the Seminary grounds and the streets of Gettysburg.

phases.title: Ewell's corps and the XI Corps come up from the north
phases.text: Two divisions of Ewell's corps came down on the town from the north while the XI Corps hurried up. Rodes's and Early's divisions then assaulted and outflanked the I and XI Corps north and northwest of the town.

phases.title: The Union line falls back to Cemetery Hill
phases.text: Howard ordered a retreat to Cemetery Hill, and the I Corps was driven back through the Seminary grounds and the streets of Gettysburg.

phases.title: The Union line forms a fishhook
phases.text: Most of the Union infantry reached the field. The XII Corps stood on Culp's Hill, the remnants of the I and XI Corps on Cemetery Hill and the II Corps on Cemetery Ridge. Longstreet's corps came up to attack the Union left.
phases.when: Evening of 1 July to the morning of 2 July

phases.title: Sickles's corps meets Longstreet's attack
phases.text: Sickles had advanced the III Corps west to the Emmitsburg Road, away from Cemetery Ridge. Longstreet's divisions came forward and found it directly in their path.

phases.title: Hood attacks Devil's Den and Little Round Top
phases.text: Meade sent in the V Corps among other reinforcements. Hood's division moved further east than intended and attacked Devil's Den and Little Round Top.

phases.title: McLaws overwhelms the III Corps at the Peach Orchard
phases.text: McLaws, coming in on Hood's left, drove several attacks into the thinly stretched III Corps in the Wheatfield and overwhelmed it in the Peach Orchard. The III Corps was virtually destroyed as a combat unit.

phases.title: The Pennsylvania Reserves beat McLaws back
phases.text: McLaws's attack reached Plum Run Valley before the Pennsylvania Reserves division of the V Corps, coming down from Little Round Top, beat it back.

phases.title: Pickett's Charge crosses the open ground
phases.text: After a long bombardment, Pickett's division and brigades from Hill's corps stepped off the ridge and advanced to Cemetery Ridge. To the northeast Stuart's cavalry met Gregg's division and Custer's brigade, who stopped it reaching the rear of the Union infantry.

phases.title: The charge is repelled at the Angle
phases.text: The Union line wavered and broke for a time at the Angle, but reinforcements rushed into the breach and the Confederate attack was repelled. Nearly half of the attackers did not return to their own lines.

note: The battle lasted three days (1 to 3 July 1863) and the plan draws it at the scale of corps on one plan, so distances are not to scale: the accounts put the two ridges about a mile apart. Positions on the town side and the lie of the hills are placed by judgement from the directions the accounts give. Ewell's attacks on Culp's Hill and East Cemetery Hill on 2 July and the cavalry action southwest of town are left out. The accounts do not say what became of Buford's cavalry after the first morning, so it is taken off the plan once the I Corps has fallen back.
